newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to oppose bringing labour under WTO ambit.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to oppose bringing labour under WTO ambit.

text.p: Pakistan will reject attempts to bring labour and investment issues under discussion at the World Trade Organisation (WTO) ministerial meeting next week, the caretaker commerce minister said on Wednesday.

Zubair Khan told a news conference Pakistan believed labour issues should be dealt with by the International Labour Organisation (ILO) and investment issues by the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD).

"Labour should be dealt with by the ILO and the investment issues should be dealt with by the UNCTAD," said Khan, who will represent Pakistan at the first ministerial conference of the 125-member World Trade Organisation in Singapore.
"By and large most developing countries have this stand. Even some industrial countries stand with us," he said.
India, Malaysia and Indonesia also reject any WTO discussion of "new issues" such as labour, investment and competition now, arguing that the WTO already has enough on its plate.
Khan said other issues on implementing WTO rules would be discussed in Singapore, including that of granting of most favoured nation status in trade to other countries.
Pakistan has been slow to grant the status to its arch-rival India, with which it has fought three wars since independence from Britain in 1947. India has already granted it to Pakistan.
Most favoured nation status is an agreement whereby two countries have to give maximum tariff concessions on their mutual trade which they already grant to other countries.

"The conference is going to look at the implementation of the WTO and on the implementation side, giving most favoured nation status will be an issue but unless India raises this I do not think this will be an issue at all," Khan said.
